subject: Literature
subcategory: Classic Novels That Changed the World
title: One Day in the Life of Ivan Denisovich
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on One Day in the Life of Ivan Denisovich.

hook.text: Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn spent eight years in Soviet labor camps and then put one single day into a novel.

buildup.text: The book described one ordinary day of freezing labor, thin soup, and tiny victories of survival.

discovery.text: Khrushchev personally approved its publication in 1962 to discredit Stalin's legacy.

twist.text: The Soviet government later banned the book and expelled Solzhenitsyn from the country entirely.

climax.text: The novel exposed the gulag system to the world and helped Solzhenitsyn win the Nobel Prize.

punchline.text: One fictional day revealed decades of real suffering.

quiz.question: Why was One Day in the Life of Ivan Denisovich initially approved for publication?
options: Khrushchev personally approved it to discredit Stalin
It was published secretly without government knowledge
